title: Rosalind and the Garden
premise: Casper Coldharbour, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps ledgers for a guild that trades in impossible things — until prayers start being answered by old gods who were supposed to be dead. When a desperate woman named Rosalind begs the guild to save her brother, a king whose crown has begun speaking with another voice, Casper discovers the gods are returning through the cracks in mortal bargains. To unbind the king, Casper must break their own oath and speak the forbidden word that once ended the age of gods, knowing it will erase every ledger they ever kept — including the record of who they are. In the end, Casper speaks it, unbinding king and god alike, and chooses to remain nameless in the world's memory while Rosalind, who learned to write her own ledgers of debt and mercy, becomes the guild's new keeper.
about_author: Mirabel Sterling is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing broken contracts and unfinished wills before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people who bargain with forces larger than themselves and live to read the fine print.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the guildhouse of Vellum & Thorn, Casper audits a trade: one memory of spring, sold at winter prices. The chapter establishes the guild's rules — everything owed must be written, nothing spoken aloud. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness beneath meticulous competence.

chapters.title: A Prayer Overheard
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind kneels in a ruined chapel begging any listening power to save her brother, King Aldous, whose crown has started whispering. Something answers. She flees, terrified and hopeful, carrying an answer she never asked for. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Client Who Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Rosalind arrives at the guild disguised as a commoner, offering payment no ledger can price: a favor from something old. Casper refuses; the guildmaster accepts. Emotional beat: Casper's first crack of doubt about the rules they serve.

chapters.title: What the Crown Says
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. At court, Rosalind watches Aldous argue with himself mid-audience — his voice splitting into two cadences. The thing wearing his crown notices her noticing. Emotional beat: horror wrapped in sisterly love.

chapters.title: Swordspeaking
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Bandits ambush the party on the road to the capital; Casper speaks a blade awake from its scabbard, the last living use of the oath-craft. The sword asks them a question afterward: 'Whose oath binds you now?' Emotional beat: pride shadowed by grief for a dead order.

chapters.title: The God in the Well
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The party shelters at a village where answered prayers have gone wrong — a harvest god grants wishes literally, cruelly. Rosalind negotiates the villagers free using her own future as collateral. Emotional beat: her first taste of justice outside any law.

chapters.title: Entries Missing
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper discovers pages torn from the guild's oldest ledger — records of the last time gods answered prayers, and of the swordspeaker who ended it. Someone inside the guild is erasing history. Emotional beat: betrayal and paranoia.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Confronted, the guildmaster admits she has been trading with the returned gods for years, buying the guild's survival. She offers Casper a choice: help unbind the king and forfeit everything, or stay silent and keep their name. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Court of Whispers
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Back in the capital under false names, Rosalind works her way into the palace as a seamstress, mapping which courtiers already serve the crowned thing. She finds allies among the forgotten. Emotional beat: cunning hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Word That Ended Gods
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In a buried archive, Casper learns the forbidden word their order spoke to end the divine age — and that speaking it unmakes the speaker's recorded identity. Every ledger entry bearing their name would go blank. Emotional beat: terror of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Midnight Audience
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind reaches Aldous alone at night; for one lucid minute her brother surfaces and begs her to cut the crown from him, whatever it costs. Then the other voice returns and knows her face. Emotional beat: heartbreak and urgency.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The crowned thing sends hunters — men whose debts the guild itself holds. Casper must fight collectors bound by their own contracts, and realizes the guild is complicit in the king's binding. Emotional beat: guilt sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Debt of Blood, Debt of Name
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Cornered, Rosalind calls on the old god who first answered her — and pays part of her price: the god takes her reflection, then her childhood memories, one per favor. Emotional beat: sacrifice as agency, not victimhood.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Page
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The page-torner is revealed: Casper's own apprentice, who sold the guild's secrets to buy back his family from the crowned thing. Casper spares him and rewrites his debt instead. Emotional beat: mercy as a radical act.

chapters.title: Storming the Vault of Names
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The party raids the guild's deepest vault where the original binding contract — signed by a dying king generations ago — is stored. They retrieve it but lose the guildmaster, who stays behind to hold the door. Emotional beat: costly victory.

chapters.title: The Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Reading the contract, they learn the truth: the crowned thing is the god of oaths itself, imprisoned in the crown it was tricked into blessing. Unbinding the king frees the god. There is no clean ending. Emotional beat: moral vertigo.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind drafts her own contract — not to destroy the god or save the king cheaply, but to bind all three parties (god, crown, kingdom) to terms she writes herself. Casper teaches her the craft of binding words. Emotional beat: identity forged through authorship.

chapters.title: The Night of Long Bells
chapters.summary: POV alternating. The capital's bells ring wrong as the god strains against the crown; reality thins — prayers answer themselves, debts collect early. The city panics. The party makes its way to the throne room through collapsing certainties. Emotional beat: apocalyptic dread laced with determination.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Casper. In the throne room, Casper breaks their oath and speaks the forbidden word — but Rosalind's new contract catches the unmaking, redirecting the erasure from Casper's whole identity to the binding alone. The god leaves the crown; Aldous collapses, freed and dying. Emotional beat: climax — sacrifice averted by shared authorship, at a cost.

chapters.title: What the Word Took
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. The redirection worked imperfectly: Casper survives but their name is gone from every record, every memory except Rosalind's. Aldous lives, diminished, abdicating to a council. Emotional beat: tender grief for what cannot be restored.

chapters.title: The New Keeper
chapters.summary: POV Rosalind. Rosalind rebuilds the guild around her own principles — debts that can be forgiven, trades that require consent. She keeps two ledgers: one for the world, one private, in which she writes Casper's name daily so it is never fully lost. Emotional beat: justice institutionalized as care.

chapters.title: The Garden
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Nameless and free, Casper tends a walled garden behind the rebuilt guildhouse — the one impossible thing never traded away. Rosalind visits, reads them their own name from the private ledger, and for a moment the world remembers. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — identity as something given, renewed, and chosen.
